title: Run the current shell from YEIS universe/system data behind a reversible engine switch

scope.subject: Observation-first YEIS model bridge into current Galaxy/System UI

research_summary: Phase 2 transfers system-data authority without replacing rendering yet. The verified MIT YEIS snapshot provides the real HYG star catalog, deterministic system generation and Hero ExtraSystem registry, but code inspection confirms that this old MIT snapshot does not include a general NASA confirmed-exoplanet catalog. Therefore an unqualified YEIS-only bridge would regress the project's known-astronomy rule by replacing confirmed planets with generated ones. The correct bridge is observation-first: retain the existing NASA Exoplanet Archive snapshot for confirmed nearby host systems, use YEIS HYG stars and deterministic systems for other real stars, and use the YEIS Hero registry for AURORA. Expose this only under ?engine=yeis until render/camera migration is complete. The existing R3F scenes remain display adapters and V2 remains the default fallback.

sources.finding: YEIS Universe exposes real catalog stars, deterministic procedural stars/systems and hand-made ExtraSystem exceptions, providing the model authority for non-observed systems.
At the selected MIT snapshot, ordinary non-Solar star systems are deterministically synthesized from StarInfo; the source does not integrate the general confirmed NASA exoplanet catalog.
NASA Exoplanet Archive TAP/API remains the authoritative reusable source already used by the project for confirmed planetary-system parameters.

StarCatalog provides 109,401 HYG-derived real stars with names, positions, magnitudes, color indices and derived physical parameters; namedIndices gives a practical bright named subset for interactive migration.
The current R3F display layer can continue consuming ordinary marker objects and built-in pointer interactions while model authority migrates independently.

search_ladder.conclusion: YEIS remains the selected mother, but switching its full renderer now would combine model and visual migration in one risky step.
A model bridge can expose YEIS catalog/system results through the existing shell types and preserve a reversible engine switch.
NASA confirmed systems must remain an observation override above YEIS deterministic generation; this preserves known astronomy while reusing both mature sources.
Use a small bright/named HYG marker subset for clickable migration; do not prematurely render every one of the 109,401 catalog stars as interactive objects.

coverage_matrix.capability: confirmed exoplanet parameters stay observed rather than generated
coverage_matrix.decision: NASA catalog systems remain higher-priority overrides; YEIS fills real stars that lack an observed-system override.
For HYG markers, system resolution must call Universe.system(starId) and convert its bodies instead of invoking the local V2 generator.

coverage_matrix.capability: Hero AURORA uses the selected mother registry
coverage_matrix.decision: The bridge resolves AURORA from the proven ExtraSystem registration rather than maintaining a second Hero system definition in V2.
Keep V2 default and select the new model with a query switch until visual/camera parity is proven.
Translate mother-model outputs to the existing SystemDefinition/PlanetDefinition display contracts during this phase.

candidates.name: NASA observed systems > YEIS HYG/system model > YEIS Hero registry, behind ?engine=yeis
candidates.license: MIT core + NASA public scientific data + HYG CC BY-SA attribution
candidates.reason: Migrates actual model authority while preserving confirmed astronomy, Hero overrides and a rollback path; current rendering can remain unchanged for this phase.

candidates.name: Use YEIS HYG + deterministic systems for all real-star markers
candidates.reason: Simpler, but the selected MIT snapshot generates ordinary planets and would overwrite known confirmed-exoplanet information already available from NASA.

candidates.name: Replace current Galaxy/System renderer with the full YEIS render loop immediately
candidates.license: MIT pinned source; third-party notices retained
candidates.reason: Eventually useful but combines data, camera, renderer and UI integration in one step before the model bridge has isolated semantic differences; poor rollback granularity.

candidates.name: Keep the local V2 star/system generator as the active model
candidates.reason: Would preserve current behavior but defeat the accepted mother-engine decision and leave two competing universe models indefinitely.

candidates.name: Expose all 109,401 HYG catalog stars as current interactive markers immediately
candidates.reason: Model migration does not require making every real star a clickable R3F object; use a bright named subset now and migrate the dedicated star renderer later.

decision.rationale: Move system-data authority to the selected YEIS mother while explicitly keeping NASA confirmed exoplanet systems as a higher-priority observation override. Run the bridge behind ?engine=yeis so the current rendering shell can validate semantics independently from the later camera/render migration.

higher_level_tradeoffs.reason: The full renderer is broader but couples four migration axes at once; the reversible model bridge produces more diagnostic value per change and does not create throwaway model work.

decision.fallback: If a mapped YEIS system cannot be represented by current display types, keep that object on the V2/NASA path and record the missing body/orbit type for the renderer migration instead of simplifying mother data.
